slides.title: Historical Figures and Legacy
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 8 English, Unit 7: Historical Figures and Legacy. In this unit, you will explore the theme of Historical Figures and Legacy - a topic that invites you to think about how individuals shape history and how their actions echo through generations. The centrepiece is an original story, "The Rebellion of Silence", which follows Jamal, a quiet but determined student at an East African boarding school in 1948, as his anonymous essays challenge an unjust ban on debate. Alongside the story, you will master the grammar of narrating the past - Past Simple and Past Continuous, the Past Perfect, reported speech, verbs with prepositions, phrasal verbs, reflexive pronouns, time phrases and discourse markers - and build a rich vocabulary for discussing argument, leadership, emotion and change. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use the Past Simple and Past Continuous tenses correctly to narrate events and describe actions in progress in the past.
Form and use the Past Perfect tense to show which action happened first when telling a story.
Convert direct speech into Reported Speech, adjusting pronouns, verb tenses, and word order correctly.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use the Past Simple and Past Continuous tenses correctly to narrate events and describe actions in progress in the past. You will also form and use the Past Perfect tense to show which action happened first when telling a story. You will also convert direct speech into Reported Speech, adjusting pronouns, verb tenses, and word order correctly. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: benign, reprieve, defect, disposition, systematic, cache. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Storyteller's Toolkit: Talking About the Past
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Legacy: The People History Remembers and The Storyteller's Toolkit: Talking About the Past. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
bullets: The Past Simple reports a finished action, while the Past Continuous shows an action in progress across time; used together, they let one event interrupt...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Past Simple vs Past Continuous. The Past Simple reports a finished action, while the Past Continuous shows an action in progress across time; used together, they let one event interrupt another in a story. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1: The Rebellion of Silence Retold
Writing 1: Narrative Essay -- A Lasting Legacy
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: The Rebellion of Silence Retold. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
